title: What must be added to 250 to reach -100?
description: A take away of positive two hundred fifty from negative one hundred is read as a missing number problem. On a line with only zero marked, the walk from two hundred fifty to negative one hundred gives the missing number. Keeko's doubt is that the missing number is positive.
teaching_notes: One idea: negative one hundred take away positive two hundred fifty is the number to add to two hundred fifty to reach negative one hundred, found by walking on the line. Watch for students who give the distance with a plus sign and forget that the walk goes left.

source: The following UNL shows a subtraction problem which can also be written as a missing addend problem: (-100) - (+250) = ? or 250 + ? = -100.
video_script.why: The child reads a take away as a missing addend problem, and finds the missing number by walking from one number to the other on a line with only zero marked.
video_script.substitution: The book's own line with only zero marked, for (-100) - (+250) and 250 + ? = -100.
video_script.anchor: the line of the book with only zero marked, with 250 to the right of zero and -100 to the left
video_script.wrong_answer: the missing number is positive three hundred fifty
video_script.wrong_move: gives the distance between the two numbers and writes it as positive, without noticing that the walk is to the left
video_script.payoff_line: The missing number is negative three hundred fifty.

final_answer.spoken: the missing number is negative three hundred fifty

maths_rules: from 250 left to 0 is 250 steps backward; from 0 left to -100 is 100 more steps backward
slip: +350 from 250 goes right to 600, not -100
video_script.design: A line with only zero marked; 250 is marked to the right, -100 to the left, and one arrow runs from 250 to -100 in two parts.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a line with only 0 marked; the take away (-100) - (+250) = ?

marks.scene: the title card arrives and a line with only 0 marked is drawn
marks.ask: the take away (-100) - (+250) = ? is written above the line

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a line with only zero marked.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is negative one hundred take away positive two hundred fifty?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.rule: the line Target number = Starting number + Movement is written
marks.term: the blank in 250 + ? = -100 is circled and named

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>A take away asks for the movement needed, and the target is the start plus the movement.
<bookmark mark='term'/>The number we must add to reach the target is called the missing addend.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, negative one hundred take away positive two hundred fifty.

marks.find: the words missing addend are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the missing addend.

marks.same: 250 + ? = -100 is written beside the take away

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, write it as a missing addend problem. Two hundred fifty plus what gives negative one hundred?

beats.on_screen: mark 250 to the right of 0 and -100 to the left of 0

marks.mark: 250 is marked to the right of 0 and -100 to the left of 0

narration: <bookmark mark='mark'/>Step two, mark two hundred fifty to the right of zero, and negative one hundred to the left.

beats.on_screen: walk left: 250 steps to 0, then 100 more steps to -100

marks.first: an arrow of 250 steps runs left from 250 to 0
marks.second: the arrow goes on 100 steps left from 0 to -100

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, walk from two hundred fifty to zero, which is two hundred fifty steps backward.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Then go one hundred more steps backward, to negative one hundred.

marks.ans: the whole arrow is labelled -350 and boxed
marks.pay: the sentence is written under the check

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The whole walk is three hundred fifty steps backward.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check it, two hundred fifty plus negative three hundred fifty is negative one hundred.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>The missing number is negative three hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 250 + 350 = 600 shown to the right of 250; struck out; the arrow to the left of 0 lights up

marks.doubt: the number with a plus sign is written and an arrow runs right from 250
marks.fix: the arrow is struck out and the left arrow lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the missing number is positive three hundred fifty, because that is the distance.
<bookmark mark='short'/>Two hundred fifty plus positive three hundred fifty is six hundred, which is far from negative one hundred.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The walk goes to the left, so the number must be negative.
